correctness.rationale: The two local hub-conditioned maps are AND and OR of the rim neighbours; the exact two-step compositions force full parity classes when the hub is constant, and forbid isolated ones in each step-two component when the hub switches. Weighted cyclic run enumeration, with a separate full-word term and L=2 convention, gives the claimed coefficient formula for all n>=3. The two strict hub inequalities are necessary and sufficient, and one zero-hub phase identifies each switch cycle uniquely. The Goles–Olivos theorem excludes longer periodic orbits. All labelled states were enumerated independently through n=14 using the included standalone checker; finite checks support but do not substitute for the all-n proof.

value.rationale: Wheel graphs are a natural smallest hub-plus-local-ring family where a single globally connected majority voter interacts with local rim updates. Exact recurrent-state classification across every wheel size is a motivated dynamical invariant. The nontrivial all-size run polynomial separates hub-preserving and hub-flipping oscillations, isolates n=4 as the only size without hub switching, and gives all primitive two-cycle counts rather than a generic period bound. It offers a controlled benchmark for qualitative and numerical network dynamics without pretending to characterize arbitrary graphs.
